Year 2: Core domains — Cognitive Psychology, Developmental Psychology, Social Psychology, Biological Psychology, Personality and Individual Differences; laboratory practicals (100 hours)
Year 3: Advanced topics — Abnormal Psychology, Clinical Psychology, Health Psychology, Organisational Psychology; research apprenticeship with faculty (optional); 200-hour internship
Year 4: Specialisation tracks — Clinical Psychology Preparation, Organisational Psychology, Cognitive Neuroscience, or Educational Psychology; honours thesis (12 credits) or applied research project
Research facilities: HKU Psychology Laboratory with eye-tracking (Tobii Pro), EEG (Neuroscan), behavioural observation suites, and virtual reality equipment for anxiety research
Accreditation pathway: Curriculum accredited by Hong Kong Psychological Society (HKPS); graduates eligible for HKPS graduate membership and professional training programmes
Interdisciplinary options: Minor in Neuroscience, Counselling, or Data Science; joint research with HKU Brain Health Institute and Faculty of Medicine

Educational Psychology: PGDE + Master's in Educational Psychology; work at Education Bureau, school-based support teams, or special education centres
Organisational Psychology: HR analytics, talent management, organisational development at multinational corporations (HSBC, Google, Amazon); starting salaries HK$25,000-35,000/month
Research & Academia: PhD at HKU, CUHK, or overseas (Stanford, Yale, UCL); postdoctoral positions at HKU Brain Health Institute or overseas universities
Counselling & Mental Health: Counselling psychologist at community centres, youth services, family planning associations; Master's in Counselling enhances prospects
Marketing & Consumer Research: Consumer insights, UX research, brand strategy at Nielsen, Ipsos, Meta, or advertising agencies; psychology-trained researchers highly valued
Psychology facilities: The Jockey Club Tower houses dedicated psychology laboratories, observation rooms with one-way mirrors, and group testing suites
Research centres: HKU Centre for Cognitive and Brain Sciences, Centre for Suicide Research and Prevention, Centre for Family and Population Research — students can volunteer or assist
Libraries: Main Library psychology collection (100,000+ volumes); online access to PsycINFO, PubMed, Web of Science; dedicated psychology subject librarian
Student societies: Psychology Society organises academic seminars, mental health awareness campaigns, peer mentoring; active collaboration with Counselling Centre
Wellness support: HKU Counselling and Person Enrichment Centre (CPEC) provides free counselling services; psychology students often shadow practitioners as part of career exploration
Admission statistics: ~900 applicants for ~180 places (5:1 ratio) — highly competitive due to popularity of psychology and limited places
Score distribution: 70% of admitted students score 29-33 points; students with 27-28 need exceptional personal statement or psychology-related experience
Subject relevance: Biology Level 5+ advantageous for neuroscience track; Economics Level 5+ for organisational psychology; English Level 5+ essential for all applicants
Comparison with CUHK Psychology (JS4046): HKU has stronger research output (h-index) and clinical psychology training links; CUHK has larger intake (~250 places) and broader social science context
Non-JUPAS intake: ~20% of places for international students, particularly from mainland China and Southeast Asia, raising cohort academic standards
Trend: Post-pandemic surge in mental health awareness has increased applications by 25% since 2020; clinical psychology pathway now requires ~32 points median

bullets: Minimum DSE requirements: 4 core subjects + 2 electives with Level 3 in English and Chinese, Level 2 in Maths and Liberal Studies; Chemistry and Biology mandatory
Typical admission score: median 32 points (Best 6 subjects), lower quartile ~30, upper quartile ~34
Subject requirements: Chemistry Level 5+ and Biology Level 5+ strongly preferred; Physics or Mathematics (M1/M2) advantageous for biophysics and bioinformatics pathways
Interview: Required for shortlisted candidates — assesses scientific reasoning, understanding of biomedical research, motivation for laboratory careers, and ethical awareness
Alternative entry: IB (32+ points with Chemistry and Biology HL), GCE A-Level (AAA including Chemistry and Biology), SAT (1350+) with AP Biology and Chemistry

Year 3: Advanced research training — Research Methods in Biomedicine, Bioinformatics, Drug Discovery and Development; 400-hour research placement in HKU medical research labs or partner institutions

Clinical exposure: Shadowing opportunities at Queen Mary Hospital pathology labs, clinical genetics service, and diagnostic microbiology units; 40 hours clinical observation minimum
Accreditation: Programme aligned with Institute of Biomedical Science (IBMS, UK) standards; graduates eligible for IBMS accredited training portfolio

Healthcare & Public Health: Scientific officer at Department of Health, Centre for Health Protection, or Food and Environmental Hygiene Department; public health research roles
Medical Writing & Regulatory Affairs: Medical writer, regulatory affairs associate at pharmaceutical companies or CROs (IQVIA, PPD); requires strong scientific communication skills
Further Studies: Master's (MPhil/PhD) in Biomedical Sciences, Medicine (MBBS via graduate entry), Dentistry, or Veterinary Science; strong research portfolio essential for competitive programmes

Laboratories: BSL-2 and BSL-3 containment facilities, cell culture suites, molecular biology labs, histopathology unit, and imaging centre with confocal and electron microscopes
Research centres: HKU-Pasteur Research Pole (infectious diseases), Centre for Cancer Research, Stem Cell and Regenerative Medicine Consortium — students can join as research assistants from Year 2
Libraries: HKU Medical Library with 200,000+ biomedical volumes; online access to Nature, Science, Cell, Lancet; interlibrary loan with partner hospitals
Student life: Biomedical Sciences Society organises lab skills workshops, career talks with industry scientists, hospital visits, and annual research symposium

JS6114.nameEn: Bachelor of Science in Exercise and Health

bullets: Minimum DSE requirements: 4 core subjects + 2 electives with Level 3 in English and Chinese, Level 2 in Maths and Liberal Studies; Biology or Physical Education preferred
Typical admission score: median 26 points (Best 6 subjects), lower quartile ~24, upper quartile ~28 — accessible to students with strong interest in sports and health
Preferred electives: Biology (for physiology pathway), Physical Education (demonstrates practical sports background), Chemistry, or Combined Science; no strict subject requirements
Interview: Required for shortlisted candidates — assesses sports participation history, understanding of exercise science, communication skills, and motivation for health promotion careers
Alternative entry: IB (26+ points), GCE A-Level (BBB), relevant sports coaching diplomas with outstanding athletic achievements, elite athlete admission scheme
Year 1: Foundation sciences — Human Anatomy, Exercise Physiology, Biomechanics, Nutrition for Health; sports skill development modules; 40 hours practical coaching experience
Year 2: Core exercise science — Motor Learning and Control, Sports Psychology, Health Assessment and Fitness Testing, Strength and Conditioning; laboratory practicals (120 hours)

Year 3: Specialisation tracks — Clinical Exercise Physiology (cardiac rehabilitation, diabetes management), Sports Performance (athlete training, talent development), or Health Promotion (community wellness, corporate health); 300-hour internship

Year 4: Advanced practice — Exercise Prescription for Special Populations, Research Methods in Exercise Science, Sports Management; honours project or community health programme; 400-hour capstone placement
Practical facilities: HKU Stanley Ho Sports Centre with exercise physiology lab, biomechanics motion capture suite, strength and conditioning gym, swimming pool, and outdoor sports fields

Accreditation pathway: Curriculum aligned with American College of Sports Medicine (ACSM) and Exercise & Sports Science Australia (ESSA); graduates eligible for certified exercise physiologist registration
Interdisciplinary options: Minor in Public Health, Nutrition, or Psychology; joint projects with HKU Medical School and School of Public Health

Clinical Exercise Physiology: Cardiac rehabilitation specialist at HA hospitals, diabetes exercise programmes at private clinics; requires ACSM Certified Clinical Exercise Physiologist (CCEP); starting salaries HK$25,000-35,000/month

Sports Performance: Strength and conditioning coach for Hong Kong Sports Institute (HKSI), professional sports teams (football, rugby, cricket), or private athletic training centres; HK$20,000-40,000/month depending on athlete level

Health Promotion & Corporate Wellness: Wellness programme manager at corporations (banks, insurance companies), community health centres, or NGOs (Hong Kong Cancer Fund, Heart Foundation); HK$22,000-32,000/month
Physical Education Teaching: PE teacher via PGDE (Primary or Secondary) at HKU Faculty of Education; requires teaching practice and registration with Education Bureau
Sports Administration & Management: Programme coordinator at National Sports Associations (HK Football Association, HK Rugby Union), event management at Hong Kong Sports Association for the Disabled
Further Studies: Master's in Sports Science (CUHK, HKU), Exercise Physiology (overseas), or Public Health; PhD for academic and research careers in exercise science
Sports facilities: Stanley Ho Sports Centre — 5-minute walk from Main Campus; features Olympic-standard swimming pool, athletics track, tennis courts, squash courts, fitness centre, and sports hall

Exercise science labs: Exercise physiology lab with metabolic carts (VO2 max testing), lactate analysers, ECG systems; biomechanics lab with 3D motion capture (Vicon) and force plates; body composition lab (DEXA, BOD POD)
Teaching spaces: Dedicated sports science teaching labs, seminar rooms with video analysis software (Dartfish), and outdoor practical teaching areas
Student societies: Physical Education and Sports Science Society organises sports competitions, coaching workshops, first aid certification courses, and annual sports science conference
Location advantage: Stanley Ho Sports Centre adjacent to Main Campus; easy access to Hong Kong Sports Institute (Sha Tin) for elite athlete placements and HKSI coaching mentorship
Admission statistics: ~400 applicants for ~80 places (5:1 ratio) — moderate competition; many applicants have strong sports backgrounds rather than purely academic scores
Score distribution: Broad range 22-28 points accepted; holistic review emphasises sports achievements, leadership in physical activities, and genuine interest in health promotion
Athlete premium: Elite athletes (HKSI squad members, national team representatives) receive significant admission preference even with scores below median; HKU has dedicated athlete admission scheme

Comparison with CUHK Sports Science (JS4324): HKU has stronger clinical exercise physiology focus and medical school links; CUHK has larger intake (~120 places) and broader sports management curriculum
Non-JUPAS intake: ~15% of places for international students and mature applicants with sports coaching or fitness industry experience
Trend: Growing demand post-pandemic for health and wellness professionals; corporate wellness sector expanding rapidly in Hong Kong; 2024 applications up 15%

bullets: Minimum DSE requirements: 4 core subjects + 2 electives with Level 3 in English and Chinese, Level 2 in Maths and Liberal Studies; Chemistry and Biology strongly preferred
Typical admission score: median 27 points (Best 6 subjects), lower quartile ~25, upper quartile ~29 — accessible for students with strong science foundation
Preferred electives: Chemistry (essential for food chemistry), Biology (for nutrition physiology), Combined Science, or Health-related Applied Learning subjects
Interview: Not required for standard admission; portfolio of nutrition-related activities (cooking competitions, health promotion projects) may strengthen borderline applications
Alternative entry: IB (27+ points with Chemistry and Biology), GCE A-Level (ABB including Chemistry), relevant food science diplomas with distinction
Year 1: Science foundation — General Chemistry, Organic Chemistry, Biology, Biochemistry, Introduction to Food Science; laboratory skills in food analysis and microbiology (80 hours)
Year 2: Core nutrition and food science — Human Nutrition, Food Chemistry, Food Microbiology, Nutritional Biochemistry, Food Processing and Technology; sensory evaluation practicals

Year 3: Advanced topics — Clinical Nutrition, Community Nutrition, Food Safety and Quality Management, Sports Nutrition, Paediatric Nutrition; 250-hour internship at hospitals (QMH dietetics), food companies (Nestle, Vitasoy), or government laboratories

Year 4: Specialisation and research — Food Product Development, Research Methods in Nutrition, Public Health Nutrition; honours research project (12 credits) or industry capstone; optional study abroad at University of Queensland or Wageningen University

Laboratory facilities: Food chemistry lab (HPLC, GC-MS), microbiology lab (food pathogen testing), sensory evaluation suite ( booths with controlled lighting and temperature), pilot food processing plant
Accreditation: Programme accredited by Hong Kong Nutritionists Society (HKNS); graduates eligible for Registered Dietitian (RD) pathway via accredited Master's programme
Interdisciplinary options: Minor in Public Health, Food Safety, or Business; joint research with HKU School of Public Health and Food and Health Bureau

Registered Dietitian: Master's in Dietetics required for RD registration; work at HA hospitals (Queen Mary, Prince of Wales), private clinics, or long-term care facilities; starting salaries HK$28,000-38,000/month after registration
Food Industry: Food technologist, quality assurance manager, product development scientist at Nestle Hong Kong, Vitasoy, Lee Kum Kee, or food startups; starting salaries HK$22,000-30,000/month

Government & Public Health: Scientific officer at Food and Environmental Hygiene Department, Centre for Food Safety; nutrition policy advisor at Food and Health Bureau; public health nutrition programmes

Community & Wellness: Nutrition educator at NGOs (Hong Kong Cancer Fund, Diabetes Hong Kong), corporate wellness programmes, school lunch programme coordinator
Further Studies: Master's in Food Science (CUHK, overseas), Public Health Nutrition (UK, Australia), or PhD in Nutritional Sciences; academic careers in teaching and research
Science facilities: Kadoorie Biological Sciences Building and James Hsioung Lee Science Building with dedicated food science laboratories and nutrition research suites

Specialised labs: Food chemistry laboratory with chromatography equipment, food microbiology containment lab (BSL-2), sensory evaluation suite with 12 individual booths, pilot-scale food processing equipment (extruder, spray dryer, retort)
Research centres: Centre for Food Safety and Technology Research, collaborating with Food and Environmental Hygiene Department; nutrition intervention studies with HKU School of Public Health
Libraries: Main Library food science collection; online access to Journal of Nutrition, Food Chemistry, Appetite; database access to Food Science and Technology Abstracts (FSTA)
Student societies: Food and Nutritional Science Society organises cooking workshops, nutrition awareness campaigns, industry visits to food factories, and annual food innovation competition
Admission statistics: ~500 applicants for ~100 places (5:1 ratio) — moderate competition; smaller programme with strong industry and professional links

Geography facilities: The Jockey Club Tower houses dedicated GIS laboratories, map library (50,000+ maps and aerial photographs), and physical geography teaching labs
GIS Laboratory: 40 workstations with ArcGIS Pro, QGIS, ENVI, ERDAS Imagine, Google Earth Engine; high-performance computing for spatial analysis; drone fleet for aerial surveying

Map library: One of Hong Kong's largest cartographic collections including historical maps of Hong Kong, China, and Southeast Asia; aerial photograph archive dating to 1924
Student societies: Geography Society organises field trips, map-making competitions, urban exploration walks, and career talks with planners and environmental consultants

JS6117.nameEn: Bachelor of Science in Marine Biology

bullets: Minimum DSE requirements: 4 core subjects + 2 electives with Level 3 in English and Chinese, Level 2 in Maths and Liberal Studies; Biology mandatory, Chemistry strongly preferred
Typical admission score: median 25 points (Best 6 subjects), lower quartile ~23, upper quartile ~27 — one of the more accessible science programmes at HKU
Preferred electives: Biology (essential), Chemistry (for marine chemistry and pollution studies), Geography (for coastal processes), or Combined Science; Marine-related Applied Learning accepted
Interview: Not required for standard admission; portfolio of marine conservation volunteering, diving certifications, or environmental projects may strengthen application
Alternative entry: IB (25+ points with Biology HL), GCE A-Level (ABB including Biology), SAT (1200+) with AP Environmental Science or Biology

Year 1: Marine science foundation — Oceanography, Marine Ecology, Biological Oceanography, Marine Invertebrate Zoology; laboratory practicals in specimen identification and water quality analysis (80 hours); first field trip to Sai Kung marine reserve

Year 2: Core marine biology — Marine Vertebrate Biology, Marine Botany, Fisheries Science, Marine Conservation Biology; scientific diving certification (PADI Advanced Open Water + Rescue Diver); 100 hours boat-based fieldwork

Year 3: Advanced topics and research — Marine Biotechnology, Coral Reef Ecology, Marine Pollution and Management, Climate Change Impacts on Oceans; 250-hour research placement at Swire Institute of Marine Science (SWIMS) or Agriculture, Fisheries and Conservation Department (AFCD)

Year 4: Honours research — Full-time 9-month marine research project (36 credits) at SWIMS, Mai Po Nature Reserve, or overseas marine stations (Australia, Philippines, Indonesia); thesis and oral defence; target publication in marine science journals

Research facilities: Swire Institute of Marine Science (SWIMS) at Cape d'Aguilar — dedicated marine research station with wet labs, aquaria, microscopy suite, and research vessel access; only university-owned marine station in Hong Kong
Field locations: Regular fieldwork at Tung Ping Chau Marine Park, Hoi Ha Wan Marine Park, Mai Po Marshes, and offshore waters; annual overseas field camp at coral reef stations in Southeast Asia
Accreditation: Programme aligned with Institute of Marine Engineering, Science and Technology (IMarEST); graduates eligible for IMarEST membership and marine professional pathways

Marine Conservation: Marine conservation officer at WWF-Hong Kong, The Nature Conservancy, or AFCD; coral reef restoration specialist; marine protected area manager; starting salaries HK$22,000-30,000/month

Fisheries and Aquaculture: Fisheries officer at AFCD, aquaculture technologist at Fish Farming Association, or seafood sustainability consultant at Marine Stewardship Council (MSC); starting salaries HK$20,000-28,000/month

Environmental Consultancy: Marine environmental consultant at ERM, AECOM, or local consultancies; environmental impact assessment (EIA) for coastal developments; marine pollution assessment; starting salaries HK$24,000-32,000/month

Education and Research: Marine educator at Ocean Park, Hong Kong Maritime Museum, or NGO education centres; research assistant at universities or marine institutes; PhD for academic careers in marine science
Government and Policy: Scientific officer at Environmental Protection Department (marine team), AFCD fisheries management division, or Ocean Park Conservation Foundation; marine policy advisor

Further Studies: Master's in Marine Science (overseas: University of Queensland, Scripps, Woods Hole), Conservation Biology, or Environmental Management; PhD for research leadership in marine ecology or oceanography

Marine research station: Swire Institute of Marine Science (SWIMS) at Cape d'Aguilar, Hong Kong Island — 20 minutes from Main Campus; dedicated marine research facility with running seawater aquaria, microscopy suite, molecular lab, and boat mooring

Laboratories: Marine biology teaching lab at Kadoorie Biological Sciences Building (specimen preservation, dissection microscopes, water quality analysis equipment); genetics lab for marine population studies

Field equipment: Research boats (R/V Thetis), diving gear (30+ sets), underwater cameras, ROV (remotely operated vehicle), plankton nets, sediment corers, CTD profilers; maintained by SWIMS technical staff

Libraries: Main Library marine science collection; SWIMS reference library with 5,000+ marine biology volumes; online access to Marine Ecology Progress Series, Coral Reefs, Journal of Experimental Marine Biology and Ecology
Student societies: Marine Biology Society organises diving trips, beach clean-ups, marine species identification workshops, and coral monitoring volunteer programmes
Admission statistics: ~250 applicants for ~50 places (5:1 ratio) — moderate competition; smaller cohort allows intensive fieldwork and research mentoring
Score distribution: Broad range 22-27 points accepted; holistic review values marine conservation volunteering, diving experience, and genuine passion for ocean stewardship
Biology premium: Biology Level 5+ is essential for success; Chemistry Level 4+ advantageous for marine pollution and biotechnology modules; Geography helpful for coastal ecology

Comparison with other marine programmes: HKU is the only Hong Kong university offering dedicated marine biology degree; overseas alternatives (University of Queensland, James Cook University) require full international fees
Non-JUPAS intake: ~20% of places for international students, particularly from Southeast Asia and coastal regions with marine conservation interests
Trend: Growing awareness of ocean conservation and climate change impacts on marine ecosystems; 2024 applications up 15%; coral restoration and blue economy emerging career areas

WWF-Hong Kong Marine Conservation Scholarship: Full tuition for students dedicated to marine protected area management or coral reef conservation; includes WWF internship
Diving Certification Grant: HK$15,000 for PADI Advanced Open Water, Rescue Diver, and scientific diving certifications; covers equipment and training costs
Overseas Marine Research Grant: HK$40,000 for honours thesis fieldwork at overseas marine stations (Great Barrier Reef, Philippines, Indonesia); covers travel and research expenses
Get diving certified: PADI Open Water before university gives you a huge advantage; marine biology is fieldwork-intensive and diving skills open research opportunities
Volunteer in marine conservation: Join WWF-Hong Kong coral monitoring, AFCD marine park volunteer programmes, or beach clean-up organisations; demonstrates genuine commitment
Excel in Biology and Chemistry: These are the scientific core; Level 5+ in Biology is essential, and Chemistry helps with marine pollution and biotechnology modules
Visit SWIMS before applying: Arrange a tour of the Swire Institute of Marine Science at Cape d'Aguilar; understanding the research facilities strengthens your personal statement

JS6120.nameEn: Bachelor of Science in Speech and Hearing Sciences

bullets: Minimum DSE requirements: 4 core subjects + 2 electives with Level 3 in English and Chinese, Level 2 in Maths and Liberal Studies; Biology or Physics preferred for audiology pathway
Typical admission score: median 28 points (Best 6 subjects), lower quartile ~26, upper quartile ~30 — competitive due to professional registration pathway
Preferred electives: Biology (for anatomy and physiology), English (for language analysis), Psychology, or Linguistics; strong communication skills essential

Interview: Required for shortlisted candidates — assesses communication clarity, empathy, understanding of speech therapy profession, and motivation for helping individuals with communication disorders
Alternative entry: IB (28+ points), GCE A-Level (ABB), relevant healthcare or education diplomas with outstanding performance, mature applicant scheme for experienced teaching assistants

Year 1: Foundation sciences — Anatomy and Physiology of Speech and Hearing, Phonetics and Phonology, Introduction to Linguistics, Developmental Psychology; 40 hours observation at speech therapy clinics

Year 2: Core speech and hearing sciences — Speech Science, Hearing Science, Language Development and Disorders, Articulation and Phonological Disorders; 150 hours supervised clinical practicum (diagnostic observation)

Year 3: Clinical practice — Aural Rehabilitation, Fluency Disorders, Voice Disorders, Neurogenic Communication Disorders; 300 hours direct clinical practicum with clients under supervision at HKU Speech, Language and Hearing Clinic

Year 4: Advanced clinical and research — Augmentative and Alternative Communication (AAC), Swallowing Disorders, Clinical Research Methods; 400 hours advanced clinical practicum; honours research project or case study portfolio; preparation for IASH registration examination

Clinical facilities: HKU Speech, Language and Hearing Clinic — on-campus clinic serving 1,000+ clients annually; audiology suite with sound-treated booths, audiometers, and hearing aid fitting equipment; speech science lab with acoustic analysis software (Praat, WaveSurfer)

Accreditation: Programme fully accredited by the Hong Kong Institute of Speech Therapists (HKIST); graduates eligible for registration as speech therapists (ST) with the Supplementary Medical Professions Council (SMPC)
Interdisciplinary options: Minor in Psychology, Special Education, or Gerontology; joint clinical placements with HKU Faculty of Medicine and Queen Mary Hospital

Speech Therapy: Registered speech therapist at HA hospitals (Queen Mary, Prince of Wales), special schools, private clinics, or early education centres; starting salaries HK$30,000-40,000/month after SMPC registration

Audiology: Clinical audiologist at HA hospitals, hearing aid centres, or cochlear implant programmes; requires additional Master's in Audiology for full registration; starting salaries HK$28,000-38,000/month
Education: Special education teacher with speech therapy focus; learning support coordinator at mainstream schools; educational consultant for language development programmes

Research & Academia: PhD in Communication Sciences and Disorders; research positions at universities or teaching hospitals; focus on bilingual language acquisition, autism spectrum disorders, or voice science
Private Practice: Independent speech therapy clinic owner; multidisciplinary practice with occupational therapists and psychologists; average private session fees HK$800-1,500/hour
Further Studies: Master's in Speech Therapy (overseas: UCL, University of Sydney, Northwestern University), Audiology, or Special Education; professional doctorate (SLPD) for clinical leadership

Clinical facilities: HKU Speech, Language and Hearing Clinic at Meng Wah Complex — 8 therapy rooms, 2 sound-treated audiology booths, parent observation rooms, and resource library; serves paediatric and adult clients with communication and swallowing disorders
Speech science lab: Acoustic analysis workstations (Praat, WaveSurfer), electropalatography system, nasometry equipment, laryngoscopy suite; supports research in voice science and articulation

Audiology suite: Diagnostic audiometers, tympanometers, otoacoustic emission analysers, hearing aid programming software (NOAH), real-ear measurement systems; supports hearing assessment and rehabilitation training

Libraries: Main Library speech and hearing sciences collection; online access to Journal of Speech, Language, and Hearing Research, International Journal of Language & Communication Disorders; dedicated subject librarian

Student societies: Speech and Hearing Sciences Society organises case study discussions, clinical skills workshops, volunteer visits to special schools, and advocacy events for communication accessibility
Admission statistics: ~600 applicants for ~100 places (6:1 ratio) — highly competitive due to guaranteed professional registration and strong employment prospects
Score distribution: 70% of admitted students score 26-30 points; students with 24-25 need exceptional communication skills or relevant healthcare volunteering experience
Communication skills premium: Strong English and Chinese (Cantonese) proficiency essential; interview heavily weights clarity of expression, empathy, and understanding of speech therapy role

Comparison with PolyU Speech Therapy (JS3638): HKU has stronger research focus and medical school links; PolyU has larger intake (~150 places) and more practice-oriented curriculum with earlier clinical exposure

Non-JUPAS intake: ~15% of places for international students and mature applicants with healthcare or education backgrounds; Mandarin proficiency increasingly valued for serving mainland Chinese clients
Trend: Growing demand for speech therapists due to ageing population and increased autism awareness; government expanding speech therapy services in schools and elderly care; 2024 applications up 20%

Faculty of Education Scholarship: HK$25,000-35,000/year for top 10% of cohort based on academic and clinical performance
Hospital Authority Speech Therapy Scholarship: Full tuition + HK$10,000/month during clinical years; requires 3-year HA service as registered speech therapist after graduation

Develop strong bilingual skills: Fluency in both English and Cantonese is essential; many clients are bilingual children or elderly Cantonese speakers; Mandarin is an additional advantage

Gain exposure to special needs: Volunteer at special schools, autism support centres, or elderly care homes; interviewers value candidates who understand the realities of working with communication disorders
Shadow a speech therapist: Arrange observation at HA hospitals or private clinics; understanding the day-to-day work (assessments, therapy sessions, parent consultations) strengthens your application
Prepare for the interview: Practice explaining complex concepts simply, demonstrate empathy through role-play scenarios, and research current issues (bilingualism, teletherapy, AAC technology)

Consider the emotional demands: Speech therapy requires patience, resilience, and emotional intelligence; ensure you are prepared for working with clients who may have lifelong communication challenges

最低文憑試要求：4科核心科目 + 2科選修科目，英文及中文達3級，數學及通識達2級；數學（必修部分）達4級以上至關重要，資訊及通訊科技或M1/M2高度建議
典型入學分數：中位數30分（最佳6科），下四分位數約28分，上四分位數約33分——因科技業需求而具競爭性
優先選修科目：資訊及通訊科技（ICT）、數學（M1/M2）、經濟或物理；強勁邏輯推理及編程能力至關重要
面試：標準入學不設面試；具卓越編程項目或科技比賽成就者或獲邀面試；評估技術解難及商業科技整合理解
替代入學途徑：IB（30分以上連數學或電腦科學高級程度）、GCE A-Level（包括數學達AAB）、SAT（1300分以上）連AP電腦科學或微積分
第一年：商業及科技基礎——會計學原理、經濟學、商業統計、編程導論（Python/Java）、數據庫管理系統；共同核心課程
第二年：核心資訊系統學科——系統分析與設計、數據結構與算法、電腦網絡、網頁開發、企業資源規劃（SAP/Oracle）；商業核心課程（市場、金融、營運）
第三年：進階資訊系統及專修——商業智能與分析、雲端運算、網絡安全管理、商業人工智能、區塊鏈與金融科技；於科技公司（Google、微軟、本地初創）或顧問公司（埃森哲、德勤數碼）進行300小時實習
第四年：畢業及專業實踐——資訊系統策略與管治、數碼轉型、項目管理（PMP對齊）；開發真實商業應用或為企業客戶進行顧問項目的榮譽項目；預備專業認證（AWS、Azure、PMP）
技術設施：港大商學院科技實驗室設有雲端運算沙盒（AWS、Azure、GCP）、網絡安全模擬環境、區塊鏈開發節點及配備GPU集群的人工智能/機器學習工作站
認證：課程獲AACSB及EQUIS認可；符合香港電腦學會（HKCS）及ISACA標準；畢業生符合HKCS研究生會員及CISA/CISM認證途徑資格
跨學科選項：電腦科學、數據科學或金融副修；與港大工程學院及電腦科學系聯合項目
科技顧問：埃森哲、德勤數碼或IBM科技顧問；數碼轉型專家；雲端遷移架構師；起薪每月28,000-38,000港元
